task_message:
Case L23: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 251x251x435 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case L23 is complete. Summary of what I did:

**Findings:** The T1-weighted MRI of the limb showed a large lipomatous (fat-signal) tumor: a marbled, fibrofatty mass with a long craniocaudal extent wrapping around the long bone, spanning from the volume edge at the distal end (k=0, near the joint) up to about k≈344, displacing the dark muscle bellies medially.

**Workflow:**
1. Scanned the volume with axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets and targeted single-slice views to locate the mass and rule out normal anatomy (muscle bellies, bone marrow, subcutaneous fat, intermuscular fat planes).
2. Seeded the model with positive points inside the mass at two levels (k=30 and k=160), producing a coherent 1554 mL mask covering the marbled tumor tissue.
3. Verified the boundaries in three planes at multiple levels (k=30/90/178/240/330/352), confirmed the proximal end stops correctly and the distal end reaches the volume edge.
4. Reviewed the automatic candidate proposals (C1–C3, each ~1.3–1.4 L): all three were intensity-only outlines of normal deep/subcutaneous fat surrounding the mask, so they were rejected.

**Final result:** mask saved (v2), 1554 mL, single dominant component (99.1%), confidence **medium** — the mask tracks the heterogeneous lipomatous mass well, with residual uncertainty at the thin fat-plane extension and in the most marbled (fibrous) periphery.
